items.text: 16B 1 FUEL CELLS

items.label: section_header
items.text: LEARNINGOBJECTIVES

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand that fuel cells use the energy released on the reaction of a fuel with oxygen to generate a voltage.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Knowtheelectrodereactionsthatoccurinahydrogen-oxygenfuel cell.

items.label: section_header
items.text: HYDROGEN-OXYGENFUELCELL

items.label: text
items.text: A fuel cell produces a voltage from the chemical reaction of a fuel with oxygen.Several types of fuel cells have been developed, with the most common type using hydrogen as the fuel (the hydrogenoxygen fuel cell). In this fuel cell, hydrogen is supplied externally as a gas, and the cell can operate as long as the fuel supply is maintained.

items.label: text
items.text: Other fuel cells usemethanol/ethanol orhydrogen-rich methanol as thefuels.

items.label: text
items.text: figAAhydrogen-oxygenfuel cell.

items.label: text
items.text: In the hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell (fig A), both metal electrodes are coated with platinum, which catalysesthereactionsthattakeplaceattheelectrodes.Thetworeactionsthattakeplaceinthe presence of an acidic electrolyte are shownbelow.

items.label: text
items.text: At the negative electrode:H2(g)→ 2H+(aq)+ 2e-.

items.label: text
items.text: At the positive electrode: O2(g) + 2H+(aq) + 2e-→ HzO(l).

items.label: text
items.text: The hydrogen ions (protons) pass through the proton exchange membrane, which allows them to enter the compartment containingthepositive electrode,where they canreactwith oxygen.

items.label: text
items.text: The overall cell reaction is:

items.label: formula
items.text: H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l)

items.label: text
items.text: There is also a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell that has an alkaline electrolyte. The electrode reactions for this cell are shownbelow.

items.label: text
items.text: At the negative electrode: H2(g) + 2OH-(aq) → 2HzO(l) + 2e".

items.label: text
items.text: At the positive electrode: O2(g) + H2O(l) + 2e- → 2OH-(aq).

items.label: text
items.text: The overall cell reactionis the same as above:

items.label: formula
items.text: H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(l)

items.label: text
items.text: Advantagesofhydrogen-oxygenfuelcells

items.label: list_item
items.text: .They offer an alternative to the direct use offossil fuels such as petrol and diesel.

items.label: list_item
items.text: .Unlike fossil fuels, their products do not include carbon dioxide or pollutants such as carbon monoxide and the oxides of nitrogen.

items.label: list_item
items.text: ·They are lighter and moreefficient than engines that usefossil fuels.
